minutes.headline: Finance Committee warns a large school 'restoration' override could fail, as one did in 2012.
minutes.summary: The committee heard FY27 budget presentations from the Council on Aging (level-funded), the Library (a modest increase plus a push for above-level programming funding), and Public Access Cable, which described a widening deficit from declining Comcast franchise fees and a forced studio relocation. The bulk of the meeting was a debate over the upcoming Proposition 2½ override: members worried that bundling the town's mostly level-service requests with the school committee's much larger 'restoration' budget into a single ask risks a failure like the town's 2012 override, which passed by roughly two-to-one against and led to a decade of cuts.

what_happened.line: Finance Committee members leaned toward asking voters for a trimmed, level-service Proposition 2½ override rather than bundling town requests with the school committee's larger 'restoration' budget.
The concern was explicit: a 2012 override bundled similarly and failed by roughly two-to-one, leading to a decade of cuts.
The override's shape now goes to a tri-board meeting of town and school officials on March 10.

Public Access Cable described a widening deficit from falling Comcast franchise fees and a forced studio move, and agreed to start tracking how its staff time splits between government and public-channel work.
The Council on Aging presented a level-funded budget and the Library a modest increase, with a member asking the library to itemize all funding sources next time.

why_it_matters: Whether the town bundles a school 'restoration' ask into one override question or asks for less, level-service money affects every taxpayer's ballot choice and, town officials warned, whether any of it passes at all.
Public Access Cable's declining franchise-fee revenue and relocation could affect coverage of town and school meetings if the town doesn't take up funding it.
The library's state certification and state aid depend on the town meeting a minimum appropriation threshold, which this budget cycle sets.
